_comment: Every video tutorial, keyed by the id a page names in its `video` front matter. lib/videos.mjs derives the player, key moments, transcript, VideoObject markup and video sitemap entry from this and the two WebVTT tracks, so nothing is written twice. The duration is the end of the last chapter, in whole seconds.

swift-interop.name: Osprey and Swift interop: Mac and iPhone app tutorial
swift-interop.description: A three-minute video tutorial. Osprey exports compile to a C header that Swift calls, Swift @_cdecl functions become Osprey imports, and one Xcode target ships the same app to the Mac and the iPhone.
swift-interop.posterAlt: Osprey + Swift title card with the Osprey bird, the Osprey Storage app icon and the words One app, Mac and iPhone

profiler.name: Profiling Osprey in VS Code: CPU, memory and leaks
profiler.description: A two-minute video tutorial. Run and profile the open file, read the flame graph and the heat on your source, attach to a program that is already running, then see how Osprey's memory backends work and check a program for leaks with ARC.
profiler.posterAlt: The Profiling Osprey title card with the Osprey bird and the words CPU, memory, leaks, in VS Code

package-manager.name: Add and remove Osprey packages in VS Code
package-manager.description: Browse Osprey packages, review audit warnings, add and verify a dependency, then remove it through the VS Code package workspace.
package-manager.posterAlt: The VS Code Command Palette with Osprey: Manage Packages selected.

dependent-types.name: What are dependent types?: for programmers
dependent-types.description: Types can describe facts about values. Start with a list-length example, then watch Osprey check an actual identity proof. This version is for programmers.
dependent-types.posterAlt: What are dependent types? with Osprey branding and real proof tools.

osprey-proof-kernel.name: How Osprey checks a proof: for programmers
osprey-proof-kernel.description: Follow a statement and its evidence through the proof kernel written in Osprey. This version is for programmers.
osprey-proof-kernel.posterAlt: How Osprey checks a proof with Osprey branding and real proof tools.

proof-workbench.name: Meet the proof workbench: for programmers
proof-workbench.description: Write a small argument, inspect hypotheses and goals, and complete a guided exercise in the real Workbench. This version is for programmers.
proof-workbench.posterAlt: Meet the proof workbench with Osprey branding and real proof tools.

mathlib-bridge.name: The Mathlib port is already underway: for programmers
mathlib-bridge.description: See selected imported proofs checked in Osprey and learn how the actual Mathlib Euclid import is progressing. This version is for programmers.

chromecast-from-mac.name: How to Chromecast from a Mac to a TV
chromecast-from-mac.description: A 90-second video. A native Mac player written in Osprey finds Chromecasts and Google TVs, plays an MP3 with full controls and a spectrum visualiser, and is tested end to end without a TV.
chromecast-from-mac.posterAlt: Title card with the Osprey bird and the words How to Chromecast from a Mac to a TV

static-typing-python.name: Static typing for Python-style code, with no type hints
static-typing-python.description: A 90-second video. Osprey's Python flavor infers every type and stops a mistyped call at compile time, shown on a 1,262-line Chromecast sender ported from CPython and checked against it.
static-typing-python.posterAlt: Title card with the Osprey bird and the words Static typing for Python-style code, no hints

ui-testing-by-label.name: An accessibility tree AI agents can drive: UI testing by label
ui-testing-by-label.description: A two-minute video. Osprey UI machines give every native control a role and a label; tests and agents find controls by name and press them with pointer events, with no window or browser.
ui-testing-by-label.posterAlt: Title card with the Osprey bird and the words An accessibility tree agents can drive

rust-ui-framework-without-rust.name: A Rust UI framework without writing Rust: GPUI apps as state machines
rust-ui-framework-without-rust.description: A two-minute video. Osprey UI machines describe a GPUI app as parallel state machines, a view and skins in one JSON document, with a small Osprey adapter and no layout code.
rust-ui-framework-without-rust.posterAlt: Title card with the Osprey bird and the words A Rust UI framework, without writing Rust
